evidence_summary: Gearphoria identifies UMI as United Musical Instruments, founded in 1967 by Richard Soloway. It states that UMI first made amplifiers for Gracin's Music in Freeport, New York, then began making effects including the Buzz Tone & Volume Expander, Treble-Bass Booster & Mute and Wa Pedal. This is a retrospective company-history anchor rather than a period trade document.

Effects Database explicitly catalogs a Nomad Tone Booster as "Nomad (by UMI)," establishing a direct secondary-source UMI relationship. No period primary-source scan was found in this pass, so retain as research-only rather than public-grade builder evidence.

UMI company profile states the first fuzz product was the Buzz Tone & Volume Expander and that UMI sold its pedals to hundreds of music stores. Surviving 1967-1968 examples independently anchor the product chronology.

Gearphoria identifies the Treble-Bass Booster & Mute as one of the pedals made by UMI; surviving examples include original box, manual and warranty-card evidence. Exact first production date remains open.
Gearphoria identifies the Wa Pedal among UMI-made pedals. A surviving 1969 example provides a dated period specimen anchor.
